statementIssues.note: Title says 'lighter-load power work', but OPL and VBT are defined by velocity or power targets, not lighter loads; only the mixed-training claim (C9) mentions lighter loads.

The labeled professional judgment that a session well short of failure gains less from rest redistribution leans on C21 without noting that failure was not a significant moderator in the meta-analysis itself (p20). It is labeled, so not critical.

Correctly labeled as professional judgment, but it extrapolates from a high-volume sprint pilot in amateur soccer players to a strength-and-power session window; the limitation in limitations[4] covers this.
Both leads (inter-limb asymmetry; ACL differential learning case study) are irrelevant to pre-competition dosing and add noise.

tierNote: Limited is appropriate: no source tests a session 48 hours before competition, evidence is acute, longer-term or qualitative, and recommendedDirection is correctly null with actions framed as options.
usefulnessNote: Gives an S&C coach concrete, faithfully sourced options (10% velocity loss cap, rest redistribution within 30 minutes, monitored VBT/OPL work, micro-dosing) with honest transferability caveats and clear coverage gaps; it gives no set or repetition dose and is long for a two-minute read.
suggestedDrafterFixes: When citing an author's discussion point that conflicts with or goes beyond the review's own moderator or primary analysis, include the primary result alongside it.
Keep action titles to wording the cited claims support (e.g., avoid adding descriptors like 'lighter-load' that only one claim covers).
Drop keyword-matched leads that are not topically related to the practical question rather than listing them.
Tighten bottomLine and actions length so the core options can be read in under two minutes.
